title: Efficient Bilevel Source Mask Optimization
problem: Source Mask Optimization (SMO) requires concurrent optimization of both source and mask in semiconductor lithography, but traditional sequential and alternating methods lead to slow convergence without performance guarantees.
motivation: SMO is critical for meeting the demands of advanced semiconductor technology nodes and expanding the process window in chip manufacturing.
method: In semiconductor manufacturing, creating precise chip patterns requires optimizing both the light source and the mask, but adjusting them together directly is slow and unreliable. This work reformulates the problem as bilevel (nested) optimization: alternately optimize the source while keeping the mask fixed, then optimize the mask while the source stays fixed. It uses fast forward imaging simulation—specifically accelerated Abbe imaging, which predicts how light patterns form through the mask—to quickly calculate gradients (slopes showing which direction to improve). Three different gradient-based approaches efficiently solve this nested problem.
key_novelty: The core novelty is reformulating Source Mask Optimization as a bilevel (nested) optimization problem solved with gradient-based methods.
contributions: Unified SMO framework with accelerated Abbe forward imaging
BiSMO bilevel optimization framework for concurrent source and mask optimization
Three gradient-based methods for solving bilevel SMO
40% error reduction and 8x runtime improvement over traditional methods
primary_theme: Bilevel optimization for semiconductor mask and source design
